audiences.executive: Use AI where it pays, and be able to say which models and agents run, what data they see, and what they can change.
audiences.technical: Every AI service and agent known, the tools each agent can call and what they change, prompts and answers logged, sensitive data kept out, and the models tested against misuse.
audiences.financial: Fewer AI services paid for twice by different teams, and no fine or lost customer because of an answer nobody can explain.

people: The owner of AI use or the data and AI team
Security, for agents, keys and misuse testing
Legal or compliance, for the regulation that applies
The owners of the AI use cases in production
Procurement, for the AI services teams subscribe to

objections.says: We do not use AI in production yet.
objections.clarify: Which teams pay for an AI service or call a model from their code today?
objections.answer: Most companies find AI already in use where nobody registered it: the list comes before the policy.
objections.prove: List the AI services called from your network and paid for in a month, and match them to an owner.

objections.says: Our policy already forbids pasting sensitive data into AI tools.
objections.clarify: How would you know if someone did it yesterday?
objections.answer: A policy needs a check: find sensitive data before it reaches a prompt or an index, and log what was sent.
objections.prove: Send a test prompt with invented sensitive data, and show it is caught and logged.

objections.says: Testing our models for misuse is for specialists.
objections.clarify: What could your agents change if someone gave them the wrong instruction?
objections.answer: Start with the agents that can change something, and test the instructions that should be refused.
objections.prove: Try ten instructions an agent should refuse, and record which ones it carried out.
